bull_bear.body: Regulatory tailwinds (QCO); Increasing demand for premium and luxury homes
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Cash and liquid funds of Rs. 19,510 Lakhs provide financial flexibility to fund store expansion and future growth initiatives.
- Order book of Rs. 6,240 Lakhs as of 31 March 2026 (up from Rs. 4,570 Lakhs a year earlier) supports near-term revenue visibility.
- Inventory days, excluding display stock, improved from 171 to 146 days, freeing up working capital.
- Retail capital is actively rotated rather than expanded indiscriminately - closing mature/underperforming stores while redeploying resources to higher-growth catchments.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- scale: A scalable manufacturing platform of three facilities in Bengaluru spanning over 300,000 sq. ft. with installed capacity of 3,07,200 units, including a dedicated Jigani facility for B2B — evidence: installed capacity 3,07,200 units/year across Electronic City and Jigani facilities.
- distribution: A pan-India retail network of 71 stores across 24 cities, with 48 COCO and 23 FOFO outlets and 38 stores operational for more than three years — evidence: 71 stores (48 COCO, 23 FOFO), warehouses in six major cities (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi).
- integration: Vertically integrated operations spanning raw material sourcing, product design, manufacturing, quality control and retail, supported by an in-house Design & Innovation Centre — evidence: 15,000 sq. ft. Design & Innovation Centre, a team of 150 designers and more than 1,000 skilled artisans.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Economic risk — Fluctuations in economic conditions within the Company's operating environment may create economic risks and potentially impact its sustainable growth; the Company relies on selective market expansion, complete home solutions and localisation to build resilience.
- Concentration risk — Stanley Lifestyles' reliance on the sale of sofas and recliners exposes it to concentration risk that could impact operational and financial performance; the Company is diversifying across seating, bedrooms, dining, wardrobes, kitchens and cabinetry to broaden wallet share.
- Procurement risk — Delays in the procurement of raw materials may affect timely delivery of products; the Company is increasing Indian sourcing of key raw materials, including leather, to strengthen supply-chain resilience.
- Regulatory risk — Changes in rules and regulations pose a risk to operational efficiency; the Company relies on BIS compliance and positions itself to benefit from the Quality Control Order (QCO) implementation.
- Demand/conversion risk from project handovers — The operating environment was challenging in FY26 due to delays in residential project handovers affecting conversions, alongside supply-chain disruptions and softer B2B demand.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Positioned as one of India's largest home-grown luxury/premium furniture brands with over 30 years of design, manufacturing and retail expertise (traces to predecessor 'Stanley Seating', founded 2007).
- Multi-brand, tiered portfolio spanning Ultra Luxury (Stanley Level Next, 12 stores, Rs. 5 Lakhs+ ticket), Luxury (Stanley Boutique, 18 stores, Rs. 3-5 Lakhs) and Super Premium (Sofas & More, 40 stores, Rs. 1.5-3 Lakhs) segments.
- Roughly 80-85% of retail customers are new home buyers, closely linking demand to the premium/luxury residential real-estate cycle and project-handover timelines.
- Expanding beyond furniture into a 'Complete Home Solutions' provider (kitchens, wardrobes, cabinetry, interiors) to increase wallet share per customer.
- First international foray via a strategic JV with Singer (Sri Lanka) PLC, opening Stanley Boutique Homes in Colombo (July 2026) as a platform for further global expansion.

business.body: Stanley Lifestyles designs, manufactures and retails premium and luxury home furnishings through three retail formats — Stanley Level Next, Stanley Boutique and Sofas & More — spanning ultra-luxury, luxury and super-premium segments. outlook.body:
- Continue COCO-led retail expansion, becoming more selective on catchment quality, residential-ecosystem maturity and long-term location potential rather than adding stores purely to grow footprint.
- Move Stanley's brand architecture towards becoming a complete-home solutions provider, while Sofas & More continues as a distinct furniture retail concept.
- Prepare to introduce a new format, Stanley Superlative Living, in mature markets, bringing complete-home solutions together at the high end of the luxury segment.
- Pursue international expansion beginning with Sri Lanka (Stanley Boutique, Colombo) via a joint venture with Singer Sri Lanka PLC, with plans to add five to six further locations through a shop-in-shop format.
- Simplify corporate structure via a proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries into Stanley Lifestyles Limited, to improve management efficiency, reporting and resource deployment.
- Deepen localisation of raw-material sourcing (including leather) to strengthen supply-chain resilience and cost efficiency.
- Implement new ERP and CRM platforms, targeted for FY2027, to support faster execution, stronger conversions and tighter inventory management.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Manufacturing is concentrated in two integrated facilities in Bengaluru, Karnataka (Electronic City and Jigani), together spanning over 3 lakh sq. ft. with combined installed capacity of approximately 3.07 lakh units/year; the Jigani facility is dedicated to B2B order execution. Retail expansion during FY26 added 11 new stores (COCO-led), taking the network to 71 stores (48 COCO, 23 FOFO) across 24 cities, with 5 more stores expected to commence operations shortly. The company opened its first international store (Stanley Boutique) in Colombo, Sri Lanka in July 2026, with plans to expand to five to six further Sri Lankan locations via a shop-in-shop format. New ERP and CRM systems are on schedule to go live in FY27.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural shift in the Indian furniture market towards organised and branded consumption, supported by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and premium residential development.
- Demand for the luxury/premium segment is being driven by consumer preference for aesthetically differentiated, customised, high-quality branded furniture and integrated home solutions rather than standalone products.
- Operating environment during FY26 was weighed on by delays in residential project handovers affecting conversions, alongside supply-chain disruptions and softer B2B demand.
- Company enters FY2027 with its highest-ever order book and 'encouraging traction' in full-home solutions; management expects customer conversions to strengthen as project handovers gather momentum, particularly towards the end of FY2027.
- Gross margin expansion (up 151 bps to 57.8% in FY26) attributed to localisation and restructuring initiatives; a significant share of made-to-order products keeps inventory levels low.
- The Quality Control Order (QCO), together with the company's BIS-compliant operations, is expected to further strengthen the position of organised domestic players versus furniture imports.
- Retail expansion has been selective, prioritising productivity, catchment potential and long-term relevance of each location over pure footprint growth.
- Order book increased to Rs. 624 million at the end of FY2026 from Rs. 457 million a year earlier, providing stronger revenue visibility entering the new financial year.
- Company enters FY2027 with its highest-ever order book, described as securing clear near-term revenue visibility.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural shift in the Indian furniture market towards organised and branded consumption, supported by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and premium residential development.
- Demand for the luxury/premium segment is being driven by consumer preference for aesthetically differentiated, customised, high-quality branded furniture and integrated home solutions rather than standalone products.
- Operating environment during FY26 was weighed on by delays in residential project handovers affecting conversions, alongside supply-chain disruptions and softer B2B demand.
- Company enters FY2027 with its highest-ever order book and 'encouraging traction' in full-home solutions; management expects customer conversions to strengthen as project handovers gather momentum, particularly towards the end of FY2027.
- Gross margin expansion (up 151 bps to 57.8% in FY26) attributed to localisation and restructuring initiatives; a significant share of made-to-order products keeps inventory levels low.
- The Quality Control Order (QCO), together with the company's BIS-compliant operations, is expected to further strengthen the position of organised domestic players versus furniture imports.
- Retail expansion has been selective, prioritising productivity, catchment potential and long-term relevance of each location over pure footprint growth.
- Order book increased to Rs. 624 million at the end of FY2026 from Rs. 457 million a year earlier, providing stronger revenue visibility entering the new financial year.
- Company enters FY2027 with its highest-ever order book, described as securing clear near-term revenue visibility.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Manufacturing is concentrated in two integrated facilities in Bengaluru, Karnataka (Electronic City and Jigani), together spanning over 3 lakh sq. ft. with combined installed capacity of approximately 3.07 lakh units/year; the Jigani facility is dedicated to B2B order execution. Retail expansion during FY26 added 11 new stores (COCO-led), taking the network to 71 stores (48 COCO, 23 FOFO) across 24 cities, with 5 more stores expected to commence operations shortly. The company opened its first international store (Stanley Boutique) in Colombo, Sri Lanka in July 2026, with plans to expand to five to six further Sri Lankan locations via a shop-in-shop format. New ERP and CRM systems are on schedule to go live in FY27.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- scale: A scalable manufacturing platform of three facilities in Bengaluru spanning over 300,000 sq. ft. with installed capacity of 3,07,200 units, including a dedicated Jigani facility for B2B — evidence: installed capacity 3,07,200 units/year across Electronic City and Jigani facilities.
- distribution: A pan-India retail network of 71 stores across 24 cities, with 48 COCO and 23 FOFO outlets and 38 stores operational for more than three years — evidence: 71 stores (48 COCO, 23 FOFO), warehouses in six major cities (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi).
- integration: Vertically integrated operations spanning raw material sourcing, product design, manufacturing, quality control and retail, supported by an in-house Design & Innovation Centre — evidence: 15,000 sq. ft. Design & Innovation Centre, a team of 150 designers and more than 1,000 skilled artisans.
